info.title: Origin Trace local HTTP API
info.description: Source-backed description of the Origin Trace Rust backend HTTP interface. Not a new server or a promise of full native-app parity. No credential authentication is implemented. Every /api/ request and every POST requires Host to name localhost, 127.0.0.1 or ::1 with the exact listening port; cross-site Sec-Fetch-Site is rejected. If Origin is present it must be HTTP, local, same port, without credentials/query/fragment. Nonbrowser CLI clients can omit Origin. Use local access only. Schemas explicitly marked partial retain source-specific gaps; x-max-utf8-bytes is documentary, not a standard JSON Schema validator keyword.

servers.description: Default development endpoint. Native sessions may choose an ephemeral port; use their endpoint file, do not assume 7319.

permission.description: One ordered setting for clients that let a model act. Each level names the individual flags it stands for, and the server applies exactly those. read-only, ask and auto also omit captured content from every result (--omit-content). ask and auto list the same tools: whether a person approves each effectful call is the client's own setting, and get_session_context reports the level so the model can say which applies. full adds starting, driving and ending its own live capture sessions and the content reads; its sensitive capture options also need --allow-sensitive-capture. The levels are not authorization, and the individual flags keep working on their own.

sensitive_capture.description: Under --permission full, start_live_session refuses these options before launching anything unless this flag is also set. The legacy --allow-session-start flag keeps accepting them with confirm_sensitive_capture, as before.

paused_values.description: The native debugger reads values out of a page while it is paused. Those values and the page-derived names they are keyed by are omitted below --allow-content, which --permission full implies: a property name or a paused function name can carry a secret as well as its value. The gate is content admission itself, not the --omit-content flag, so the raw-flag path (--allow-effects alone, which sets neither flag) omits them too. Identifiers, counts, origins and URLs are returned at every level, as elsewhere.

content_reads.description: Operations whose purpose is captured content (source, bytecode, disassembly and request and response bodies) are listed only with --allow-content. With it, get_source_format also lays out request and response bodies, and no result has content fields omitted below the inline limit. Larger documents still return a structural summary, so content is read in pages: get_artifact_text, get_source_format with start_line and line_count, and inspect_wasm with row_offset and row_limit. Binary responses are still refused.

session_start.title: Start a live capture session
session_start.description: Starts a new visibly labeled live capture session with named capture options: the capture browser, an Origin Trace window and every helper. When it is ready this connection moves to that session; other endpoint changes still retire the connection. Starting again first ends the session this connection started. Every option is off unless named and none is inherited from the environment. document_start permits document-start Console scripts (arming is a separate Console action). request_stacks records the call stack that started each renderer request (get_request_stack). request_content_budget_mib (1 to 4096, default 256) sets how much unique request content is kept. response_body_budget_mib (1 to 16384, default 512) sets how much unique response content is kept, and response_media also keeps element images, audio, video and fonts; both need request_content. Sensitive capture needs confirm_sensitive_capture: canvas_images, request_content (request paths, queries and bodies, request and response headers including Cookie, Set-Cookie and Authorization, each request's cookies, and response bodies) and js_invocation_digests. js_invocation_sites (a site file) or js_invocation_saved_sites (the agent sessions' own saved set) arm invocation sites. wasm_samples_per_function, wasm_samples_per_indirect_site, wasm_function_allow, wasm_function_deny and wasm_module_allowlist restrict the 16-record Wasm sample budgets and require wasm_dispatch or wasm_call_indirect. The result options and get_session_context capture_options show what the session runs with. With url, the result reports capture_observed; false means nothing was recorded, so end the session. Next: get_session_context, then get_session_summary; get_native_console for the Console. Start only for an authorized target. session_action, listed with this tool, acts only on a session this connection started. reset_wasm_sample_budgets restarts both Wasm sample indexes without a new session.

get.summary: Get compact session context and capture options

Next: get_session_summary. Debugger fields are fixed retirement values since CDP was removed. The HTTP API cannot know client effects flags: allow_effects is null; reb-api mcp fills its actual invocation admission. live_admission is availability, not authorization. Cache the context with its own ETag.

get.summary: Summarize what this capture recorded
get.description: One call that answers whether a capture worked: capture state, event counts by type, the busiest frames with their event types, session IDs, gap counts and named gap reasons, artifact counts by kind with the newest digests, and checks that name what looks wrong, such as a full sampling budget, Wasm compiled without a stored module, each artifact capture failure reason, or request bodies, full targets, header blocks and cookie lists a content session did not retain (budget, block limit, pool, channel, URL or kind) with counts, network header blocks and cookie lists that arrived for requests no longer tracked (network_headers_unattributed), requests that ended with only provisional headers (final_headers_missing, one check per reason: download, service_worker, from_cache, failed, not_reported or record_dropped), counted browser-internal exclusions, requests without a browser tab, and every request's response body case (retained, or why not: served by a service worker, reused from the memory cache, 304, redirected, aborted, cancelled, empty and the rest). Call it after get_session_context and again after an action. Counts, identifiers and origin labels only: no payloads, source, URLs paths or bodies. Covers the newest 64 MiB of events. Use get_events filters (type, frame_id, request_id) to read the records behind a count.

post.summary: Open a URL in, send input to, reset Wasm sample budgets, or end this live capture session
post.description: Drives the live session this backend belongs to. open_url opens a page in a new tab of the session's capture browser while its capture broker runs, and reports capture_observed. list_inputs, click, type, press and scroll send trusted macOS input to the capture browser's page, including cross-origin frames; they need Accessibility for the app that started the session. reset_wasm_sample_budgets restarts both Wasm sample indexes without closing the browser or starting a new capture configuration; the browser notices the reset file on its writer wake, about 250ms later. end closes the capture browser and stops the session; it stays available after capture expires; stop any Console connection first so armed document-start scripts are cleared and confirmed. Take a wait_for_events cursor before open_url or input, then wait. To run JavaScript in the page or one of its frames, use get_native_console and native_console_action. Through MCP it is listed only with --allow-session-start and acts only on a session started by that connection with start_live_session.

get.summary: get origin trace
get.description: Bounded recent evidence window: 10000 events, 30000 edges, 10000 artifacts. Optional session_id limits selection to that exact captured session. Supply it with root_process_id and root_sequence_number for an exact event. Omitted selectors remain backward-compatible only for unambiguous matches; cross-session or multiple-root matches return ambiguous without selecting a trace. A missing exact match is empty, with no fallback. An empty/ambiguous/partial document is a successful result, not a missing-resource error. Where the identity chain ends, monotonic_time_ns proximity is a separate declared correlation input: at most one cross-process record of the same request identity within 1 ms is reported as a terminal temporal_adjacency step with time_adjacent confidence. It is counted only in time_adjacent_links, never in observed_links or correlated_links, it never replaces the no_predecessor gap, and it moves neither linked_steps nor percent.

get.summary: get request headers
get.description: Header blocks of one native request per redirect hop (protocol/native-network-v3.md), from the bytes the request index names for that request, or the newest 64 MiB of events when it names none, reading at most 1024 of its records; coverage says what was read. Recorded only in sessions that retain request content. Each block gives its source (browser: provisional, before the network stack; network: as sent; early_hints: a 103), state, header count, byte length, SHA-256, and its referrer policy or status and remote endpoint. Retained blocks are read after a size and SHA-256 check and parsed into ordered headers. Values of Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, Cookie, Set-Cookie and any header whose name contains a credential root (token, secret, passw, csrf, xsrf, cookie, bearer, signature, credential, sessionid, authoriz and similar), has the whole word auth, session, jwt, otp or pwd, or has a word ending in key, except Sec-WebSocket-Key, Idempotency-Key and Public-Key-Pins are withheld as value_withheld with their byte length: like request bodies they stay in the binary artifact. Withholding goes by name, so another value, such as a Location query, is returned as captured. A hop is provisional when it has only browser request blocks.

get.summary: Fold every recorded stack of one session into one flow graph across frames, realms, JavaScript, eval and Wasm
get.description: Every request_initiator_stack (34), navigation_initiator_stack (46), async_task_stack (48) and walked script_cookie write (39) of one session, folded into one observed graph. Each distinct stack digest is decoded once and counted by occurrences; each retained script or module is read once for every frame that names it. Nodes are functions (javascript, eval for eval or new Function scripts, wasm) and sinks (request as METHOD host, navigation kind, cookie_write API), keyed by realm and code, so the same code in one realm is one node. contexts are realms: process_id plus the execution_context_id of the script_identity records (35), with the frame_ids the realm's stacks were recorded in, tab_ids and script origins. Edges: call (adjacent synchronous frames, with call sites), await (an async function's awaiter, labeled by any Promise combinator), task (a task segment: the stack that scheduled a timer, animation frame, idle callback, window.postMessage, XMLHttpRequest.send, scheduler.postTask or queued event, to that task's first frame; via names microtask hops), omitted (the run a stack deeper than 1,024 frames dropped) and request, navigation or cookie_write edges to sinks. crosses names frame (a change of realm), language (JavaScript and Wasm) and dynamic (a call into eval code). paths lists each distinct stack's edges and nodes for highlighting. A frame that does not resolve keeps its script ID and a reason; a missing scheduling stack cuts the chain (chain_cut on the node it would have entered), never bridged. Workers, MessagePort messages and out-of-process frames are not walked and are listed in not_shown. An edge counts each stack once however often that stack walks it; via, label and omitted merge what the stacks that share it say. A task edge enters only a frame known to be its task's first: the last awaiter of an await chain, else the outermost synchronous frame, never the outermost of a walk that stopped at 256 frames or of a truncated await chain. Limits are reported in limits and truncated, a scan stops at a 30-second deadline with coverage.stopped deadline, and complete is false whenever anything was cut. The answer is cached until the event store or artifact manifest changes; a deadline-cut answer is not cached. See protocol/flow-graph-v1.md.

get.summary: Read the JavaScript and Wasm call stack that started one renderer request or script navigation
get.description: Newest request_initiator_stack record (34) inside the bytes the request index names for one renderer request (or the newest 64 MiB of events when it names none), named by the renderer's process_id and request_id as its request_initiated record carries them, or with navigation_sequence the navigation_initiator_stack record (46) a browser navigation_initiator_link (47) names, or with observation_sequence one debugger observation record (40 to 45) of that renderer, with every recorded frame innermost first. JavaScript frames resolve through their script_identity record (35) and its SHA-256 to a retained JavaScript artifact of any capture origin (network, stack_script, compiled_script or dynamic_javascript), then to one-based line and UTF-16 column, artifact_line and artifact_column for Sources, and the function name the source gives at the function start. Wasm frames name their function index, module byte offset and a name-section name when the module is retained. A frame that does not resolve keeps its raw identity and a reason; nothing is guessed. A stack deeper than 1,024 frames keeps the innermost and outermost 512 with omitted frames after omitted_after_index. Await frames follow the synchronous ones. A version 2 record adds task_segments, nearest first: each async task (timer, animation frame, idle callback, window.postMessage, XMLHttpRequest.send, scheduler.postTask, queued event or observer) with the stack that scheduled it, resolved from its async_task_stack (48) artifact, and microtask hops linked through task attribution. A version 3 record adds scope, the isolate the stack was walked in (the document main thread or a dedicated, shared or service worker), message segments (MessagePort, BroadcastChannel and worker postMessage) whose frames resolve in the posting thread's or renderer's isolate, a microtask segment's promise registration (then, catch, finally or await) when promise stacks were recorded, a no_script segment that ends the chain where a task was scheduled with no script running, and an origin_rejected segment that ends it where a received message's task origin did not validate. task_chain_cut says an earlier caller was not recorded; async_callers_not_shown lists the callers this record version cannot show. status is not_recorded when the read covered the request's indexed bytes or the whole store and found no stack record, and outside_scan when it did not reach all of them; coverage says what was read. A frame keeps reason script_identity_outside_scan when its identity was not found and not every identity was read. An observation adds observation: its type, decoded detail and its own frame (the listener, timer callback or throw site) resolved alone as site, or null when it names none; its stack is the one recorded when it fired, and the site can resolve when the stack holds no script. See protocol/native-network-v3.md and protocol/native-debugger-observation-v1.md.

get.summary: Read native events, optionally filtered and paged
get.description: Without filters this is the Origin Trace UI polling window: the newest events of the last 64 MiB plus an independent network window. With any filter or cursor it scans complete records from the cursor (default: newest first), returns up to limit matches unchanged, and adds a query object with next_before and next_after cursors. Filters combine with AND. Gap fields then describe only the scanned byte range, and network_events is empty: select network records with category=network. Network requests: request_body (22) gives each body's length, type and digest, and request_target (23) the path and query only when the session retains request content; response_body (33), in those sessions only, says whether each response body was retained, partial, refused or never observed, names its response_body artifact and joins its response_started parent; select one request with request_id. request_headers (30) and response_headers (31) summarize each header block in those sessions; read them with get_request_headers. Invocation sites: js_invocation_start (24), js_invocation_settle (25) and js_invocation_request (26) give armed calls and the requests made inside them. Each also includes js_invocation beside the hex (JsInvocationDecode): status decoded with kind start, settle or request, never a value digest; status invalid has no fields. wasm_execution_outcome (27) records a trap or that an instrumented Wasm call is still executing. A sample refused by a function, module, call-site, or the 16-record stream budget is wasm_dispatch_overflow (28) or wasm_indirect_overflow (29): a compact identity, not a full observation. Payloads stay hex. wasm_dispatch_observation and wasm_indirect_observation also include wasm_observation beside that hex, decoded without an opcode workspace. status decoded names function_index, module_byte_offset, sample_index, js_invocation_state, and js_invocation_id. A dispatch object also has selector and table_count. An indirect object also has table_index, slot, callee_function_index, and resolution named resolved, null, out-of-bounds, foreign, or unresolved. callee_function_index is 0 unless resolution is resolved. status invalid carries no fields. Version 1 decodes as not observed. Any other payload version is invalid with no fields, not a version-2 prefix. The record is protocol 3, category vm, and flags 0.  wasm_dispatch_overflow and wasm_indirect_overflow include wasm_overflow beside that hex. status decoded names kind identity or omitted. An identity names ring_index, function_index, and module_byte_offset, plus selector and arm_count, or table_index, slot, and resolution. An omitted record names omitted_count and no site. status invalid carries no fields. Unknown parameters are rejected. Use a small limit through MCP and page with query.next_before.

dispatchClassification.description: Analyzer interpretation of stored artifact bytes. role.description: Derived from the record. interpreter-candidate: repeats=loop with cursor_index, cursor_pointer or frame_slot on switch_on_value, handler_table, compare_chain or threaded, unless buffer_kind is string or arguments, and unless the selector is a second-level lookup (through_lookup) on a switch or ladder; a handler table, threaded or not, reads its handler through one lookup by design. WasmObservationDecode.description: Read-path decode of one wasm_dispatch_observation or wasm_indirect_observation, placed beside the unchanged payload hex by get_events and wait_for_events. status invalid means the record was rejected and no field is returned: the envelope is not protocol 3, category vm, and flags 0; the payload version is not 1 or 2 (a later version is not returned as a version-2 prefix); or the 128-byte payload failed a wire check (nonzero reserved bytes, a broken invocation context, an unknown resolution, a callee on an unresolved entry, or any other bound). Decoding reads that record only: it does not open an opcode workspace or the module, and it does not invent a guest PC, a sample, or a caller. js_invocation_state is the stored integer: 0 not observed, 1 none, 2 inside, 3 unknown. Version 1 decodes as not observed (0, 0). js_invocation_id is nonzero exactly when the state is 2. callee_function_index is the stored index and is 0 unless resolution is resolved; that 0 is not a function index. See protocol/native-wasm-dispatch-v1.md.

JsInvocationDecode.description: Read-path decode of one js_invocation_start, js_invocation_settle or js_invocation_request, placed beside the unchanged payload hex by get_events and wait_for_events. kind names the record. status invalid means the record was rejected and no field is returned: the envelope is not protocol 3, category vm, flags 0 with an untruncated 128-byte hex payload and zero artifact, parent and navigation IDs; the payload version is not 1; or any other rule of protocol/native-js-invocation-v1.md failed. Decoding reads that record only. 32-bit and smaller integers are JSON numbers, so invocation_id joins wasm_observation.js_invocation_id directly; document_id and request_id are canonical decimal strings. Order calls by sequence_number within one (session_id, process_id), not by file order or time. No settled-value digest is decoded: digest_state only says whether one was retained. Site labels are not stored with events: get_js_invocation_sites session.sites lists what this session armed in site_slot order, each with its label.

site_slot.description: Index of the called function in the site file this session armed.

invocation_id.description: Nonzero and never reused in the renderer isolate. An invocation is (session_id, process_id, invocation_id).

parent_invocation_id.description: The invocation current when this call entered, always below invocation_id, or 0 for none. A dynamic-extent relation, not value flow.

parent_unknown.description: The invocation current at entry was a wrapper from an older configuration, so no parent is recorded. parent_invocation_id is then 0, which is not evidence of having none.

argument_count.description: Actual arguments excluding the receiver, saturating at 65535.

script_id.description: V8 script ID in this renderer process, the unit stack frames and script_compiled use.

anchor_offset.description: UTF-16 offset of the function's V8 start position: with script_id, the function a stack frame names.

source_sha256.description: The armed site's key with anchor_offset: get_js_invocation_sites session.sites names the same pair.

site_sample_index.description: This call's index in its site's 64-start budget.

sample_index.description: This call's index in the configuration's 256-start budget.

document_id.description: Digest of the DocumentToken the call ran in.

via.description: sync_return and sync_throw settle the initial synchronous extent; promise is the native promise the caller received.

value_kind.description: Wire kinds 1 to 14 in order. number is a non-integer number, object any other object, array_buffer_view a typed array or DataView.

value_length.description: UTF-16 length of a string, element count of an array, byte length of an ArrayBuffer or view; 0 for other kinds.

digest_state.description: Whether the session retained a settled-value digest. The digest itself is sensitive capture and is never returned here.

inside.description: True: script started the request while invocation_id was current. False: no script was on the stack while some admitted invocation had not settled, so which one is unknown.

invocation_id.description: Nonzero exactly when inside is true.

request_id.description: The renderer request ID of the request_initiated record written just before, as in the envelope.

Event.description: Native event record validated before HTTP delivery for protocol version, canonical identifiers, process ID, and bounded hexadecimal payload consistency. Additional native record fields remain extensible; see protocol/README.md. This schema does not yet describe every native event field. wasm_dispatch_observation and wasm_indirect_observation responses from get_events and wait_for_events include wasm_observation, and js_invocation_start, js_invocation_settle and js_invocation_request responses include js_invocation. The payload hex remains.

Exits are final for a backend.

capture_stopped.description: True only in capture_state stopped: this backend stopped the capture.

capture_controls_available.description: A live backend started with a positive broker PID. Stop signals only a running broker whose PID is still the process it named at startup.

sequence_gaps.description: Count of absent sequence IDs between observed minimum and maximum per session/process within event_window scope, including gap markers. Late arrivals close holes; duplicate IDs do not create gaps. Unknown prefixes and tails are not counted.

queue_drops.description: Sum of validated gap-record drop counts within event_window scope. May overlap sequence gaps; a bounded tail is not a whole-capture total.

network_events.description: Independent newest native-network lifecycle window within the scanned bytes. Canvas and other event categories cannot consume this window.

malformed_lines.description: Whole lines in the scanned bytes skipped because they are not valid events. Present on the polling answer. A torn tail still being written is not counted.

event_window.description: Half-open complete-record byte scope of both windows and summaries. A bounded tail excludes the older prefix and is not a session-total claim. bounded_range is a filtered read's scanned range, which can start or end inside the store.

id.description: The Traffic row identity: the renderer request when one is joined, else the browser loader.

ordinal.description: Capture order: the position at which the index first saw this request.

path.description: scheme://host[:port]/path?query with request content, host[/path] without a scheme, or the host only. Captured text: never interpret it as markup.

target.description: Captured path and query, at most 116 bytes.

status.description: The HTTP status, or failed, incomplete (observation ended or a service worker's end was lost), pending, or finished: a memory-cache reuse that carried no HTTP status, such as an MHTML archive resource (protocol/request-index-v1.md).

interrupted.description: Native observation ended (proxy destroyed or redirect handoff); the network outcome is unknown.

time.description: Milliseconds from the first to the last record, or pending.

tab_ids.description: Every tab the row belongs to: its own tab_id and the tabs of its newest request_tab_link set (protocol/native-network-v3.md). Empty is a capture error.

kind.description: request_tab_link kind: 1 dedicated worker, 2 shared worker clients, 3 service worker clients, 4 service worker last clients, 5 service worker registrant.

complete.description: Every tab_set part of the linked set was indexed.

tab_link.description: The newest request_tab_link naming this row, or null.

extension_id.description: The extension a request_extension_link names: extension traffic recorded with REB_CAPTURE_EXTENSION_TRAFFIC=1 (protocol/native-network-v3.md), else null.

tab_reason.description: Why a row with no tab and no extension has no owner, the same reason get_session_summary gives; null for a row with an owner.

root.description: request_started, else request_initiated, else the first record with a request ID.

members.description: Each session, process and request ID whose records form this row, with its record count.

first_offset.description: Record boundary of the row's first record: get_events after.

transfer_size.description: The last completion or failure record's encoded_data_length: bytes received over the network, headers included.

from_cache.description: A response_started record, or the renderer's own completion, says the response came from the HTTP cache.

from_service_worker.description: A response_started record, or the renderer's own completion, says a service worker served the response or ended the request without one (protocol/native-network-v3.md).

memory_cache.description: The row is a memory_cache_reuse record: Blink answered the load from a resource it held and made no request (protocol/native-network-v3.md).

static_data.description: A memory-cache row whose resource Blink decoded in place: a data: URL or MHTML archive resource.

race_network.description: A service worker race route: the renderer's own completion flagged from_service_worker sits on a row with browser records. failed, interrupted, status and error_code are that completion's, what the page received; the worker or the network may have answered, and the records do not say which (protocol/native-network-v3.md).

end_lost.description: A service_worker_end_lost gap names this row: the renderer lost the end of a request its service worker handled, so a row with no response reads incomplete, not pending.

memory_cache_source.description: A version 2 memory_cache_reuse names the renderer request whose response Blink reused (ResourceResponse::RequestId()). found is true only when that row exists, was requested from the reuse's web host and started before the reuse; reason says why not. A found source carries its body, which holds what was retained of the bytes Blink reused. Null for every other row and for a reuse that names none.

reason.description: Why the named row is not this reuse's load: none was recorded, it was requested from another host (a renderer process ID reused within the session), or it started after the reuse. Null when found.

mime_type.description: The response MIME type, lowercase, without parameters.

protocol.description: The negotiated ALPN protocol, such as h2.

error_code.description: The last non-zero net error code, else 0.

loader_observed.description: A browser loader record joined the request; false when only the renderer recorded it.

initiator.description: Who started the request: script or the parser in a renderer (from its request_initiator_stack), script that started a navigation (a navigation_initiator_link), a renderer without a stack record, a service worker, or the browser process; null without a versioned record.

initiator_frame.description: The innermost frame of the request_initiator_stack that names this row, resolved like get_request_stack; null without a walked stack, or for a frame past the 64 resolved per answer.

main_frame.description: A request_started record names a top-level document.

browser_internal.description: Its scheme class is browser-internal (protocol/native-network-v3.md); recorded before scheme classes, only the renderer recorded it and it names a single-label host other than localhost, as WebUI loads do.

matching.description: Requests of the snapshot that pass the filters and search.

through.description: The snapshot: requests indexed before this count.

added.description: With since: matching requests indexed at or after it.

failed.description: Failed requests in the snapshot, before filters.

sizes.description: Sums over the matching requests of transfer_size and resource_size; a request without one adds nothing.

hidden_internal.description: With hide_internal: browser-internal requests that every other filter admitted.

timeline.description: Request starts of every request the filters admit before the time range, in 120 equal buckets from the first start to the last record.

tab_id.description: A tab id, extension:<id> for one extension's traffic, or 0 for requests without an owner.

domains.description: Domains within the tab_id filter, with counts; at most 512 plus the domain filter.

epoch.description: Changes when the store is cleared or replaced and the index is rebuilt.

malformed_records.description: Network records the index could not read.

reopened.description: The index was read from its sidecar, not rebuilt.

script_id.description: Retired with CDP live scripts; always null. Kept so version 1 clients still parse the result.

side.description: Cells per side, a power of two, chosen so every window is at least min_window_bytes unless the artifact is shorter.

window_bytes.description: Whole bytes per window; windows differ by at most one byte.

min_window_bytes.description: Shannon entropy over W bytes cannot exceed log2(W), so a window shorter than the 256 possible byte values cannot reach the 0 to 8 scale.

cells.description: One byte per cell in byte order, base64. Divide by units_per_bit for bits per byte.

threshold_bits.description: A stated numeric threshold. It is not a claim that bytes are compressed or encrypted.

mixed_flag.description: Set on a cell when its window holds more than one kind.

cells.description: One byte per cell: an index into kinds, plus mixed_flag.

rows.description: Newline-terminated rows of hex byte offset, mnemonic and operands. A run of identical block openers is one row with a count suffix.

ArtifactTextPage.description: One verified page of artifact bytes. The text is captured content.

offset.description: Where this page starts, after any move to a character boundary.

next_offset.description: Where the next page starts, or null at the end.

complete.description: This page holds the whole artifact.

replacements.description: Invalid UTF-8 sequences shown as U+FFFD.

ArtifactSearchResult.description: Literal matches with bounded same-line context. Snippets are captured content.

analyzed_sections.description: Sections present in these bytes that were requested and decoded to their end.

excluded_sections.description: Sections present in these bytes that the request did not select. Their contents were not read, so nothing here is claimed about them.

truncated_sections.description: Sections present in these bytes that were requested but are not completely covered, because a limit stopped decoding or this version cannot decode them. omissions names which.

section_map_complete.description: True when traversal reached the module end, so the three lists together name every section in these bytes and a requested section absent from all three is absent from the module.

row_window.description: Present only when row_offset or row_limit was given. rows holds this window, which stops at row_limit rows or 98,304 serialized bytes.

capture_state.description: Live capture lifecycle, from the kernel lock the native event broker holds on its event store for its whole life. not_live: idle or demo backend. running: the broker is running. stop_requested: stop was delivered and the broker has not exited yet. stopped: the broker exited after this backend asked it to stop. ended: the broker exited through its own shutdown (session expiry, browser disconnect, or a failure in its log). lost: the broker is gone and left its socket behind, so it was killed or crashed. broker_connected.description: True only while a live backend's native event broker is running, including stop_requested. Idle and demo backends report false.

generation.description: Retired with CDP; always 0. Kept so version 1 clients still parse the context.

debugger_protocol_version.description: Retired with CDP; always 1. Kept so version 1 clients still parse the context.

target_document_epoch.description: Retired with CDP; always 0. Kept so version 1 clients still parse the context.

capture_epoch.description: Retired with CDP; always 0. Kept so version 1 clients still parse the context.

target.description: Retired with CDP; always null. Kept so version 1 clients still parse the context.

wasm_scripts.description: Retired with CDP; always empty. Kept so version 1 clients still parse the context.

wasm_scripts_omitted.description: Retired with CDP; always 0. Kept so version 1 clients still parse the context.

wasm_artifacts.description: Retained store inventory, not restricted or linked to a live target. May contain another session.

debugger_etag.description: Retired with CDP; always "debugger-0". Kept so version 1 clients still parse the context.

mcp_admission.description: Added by reb-api mcp only: what this connection lists and returns. permission is the --permission level, or null when the connection was started with the individual flags. None of it is authorization.

sensitive_capture.description: start_live_session may name canvas_images, request_content, response_media or js_invocation_digests. False under --permission full without --allow-sensitive-capture.

consistency.description: Historical constant: the context and the manifest tail are read independently.

capture_options.description: What this session's launcher passed to Brave, for every live session: agent, app or make live. Labels only; they grant nothing. Idle and demo backends report not_live with everything off.

request_content.description: Request paths, queries, headers and bodies, and response bodies, are retained (request_target, request_headers, response_headers and response_body events, request_body, header and response_body artifacts).

request_stacks.description: Brave walks request initiator stacks and retains their stack and stack_script artifacts (--reb-request-stacks).

document_start.description: Whether the launcher gave Brave the document-start permission. Whether this Brave honors it is document_start_supported in get_native_console.

SessionContext.description: Bounded discovery only. Titles are omitted and URL labels contain only HTTP(S) origins or conventional Wasm hex labels, not full locations. Identifiers and origins remain potentially sensitive metadata. Scripts and retained artifacts are separate inventories with no inferred association. Byte length is CDP script length when known; sha256 is populated only from validated artifact metadata. Not an authorization or retention guarantee.

ErrorCode.description: Stable bounded application reason. artifact_integrity means retained bytes no longer match the size or SHA-256 in their manifest record, so reading them again cannot help. invalid_request/state_conflict/protocol_error are coarse classifications; precise reasons are only supplied by migrated source paths. application_failed does not imply rollback or no side effects. A command-exchange timeout or lost/malformed reply uses command_outcome_unknown, not a confirmed-no-op claim. This can include interrupted queued or partial writes and does not prove a send completed.

selection_reason.description: Exact retained Traffic lookup only: stale instance/epoch, absent exact row, or duplicate public request ID. No alternative identifiers or raw diagnostics.

allowed_actions.description: Names from the embedded request contract only; never submitted values or validator diagnostics.

missing_fields.description: Names from the embedded request contract only; never submitted values or validator diagnostics.

ErrorDetails.description: Allowlisted bounded metadata only. Empty when no detail is known. No arbitrary strings, target URLs or IDs, submitted inputs, credentials, raw captures, diagnostics, or stacks. request_body timeout is before action dispatch; command_exchange uncertainty covers interrupted queued/partial writes and missing or malformed replies; it cannot establish whether an action happened. Worker termination does not undo prior effects.

AnalysisCatalog.description: Embedded current VM definitions and reviewed source context only. Match current producer ID/version and exact current_profile_digest; build identity is not recorded; historical profile definitions are not included. Digests identify content, not authenticity or correctness.

EvidencePackage.title: Origin Trace Evidence Package v1
EvidencePackage.description: Version 1 closed metadata-only evidence package. Validity establishes internal consistency of supplied untrusted metadata, not producer authenticity, capture completeness, source availability, or artifact-byte verification. Semantic checks and canonical digest rules are defined in evidence-package-v1.md.

EvidencePackageUint64String.description: Canonical unsigned 64-bit decimal, 0 through 18446744073709551615; no sign or leading zeros.

EvidencePackageInt64String.description: Canonical signed 64-bit decimal, -9223372036854775808 through 9223372036854775807; no plus sign, leading zeros, or negative zero.

EvidencePackageSelection.description: Exact selected tuple keys. Duplicate identities are rejected by bounded semantic validation; ordering is normalized for the digest.

EvidencePackageProvenance.description: Untrusted exporter assertions, not facts established by supplied-package validation. Historical producer/browser build and capture configuration are unavailable in v1.

EvidencePackageEventCoverage.description: Retained-source scan and selection assertions never establish complete capture. Runtime checks exact counts, requested/read state, scoped gaps, and applicable limitations. Limitation order is normalized.

EvidencePackageArtifactCoverage.description: Retained-source scan and selection assertions never establish complete capture. Runtime checks exact counts, requested/read state, scoped gaps, and applicable limitations. Limitation order is normalized.

EvidencePackageEventMetadata.description: Closed native metadata projection. Unknown category/type values and native gap records are not ordinary selectable events. Missing historical optional metadata is explicitly null; it is never fabricated as zero. A non-null operation requires web_audio/api_call, exact registry membership, and untruncated payload metadata.

EvidencePackageArtifactByteSize.description: Original artifact byte count as canonical unsigned decimal, at most 16777216 bytes. Artifact bytes are omitted and are not reverified by this validator.

EvidencePackageArtifactMetadata.description: Closed artifact metadata projection. The verification string is an untrusted export-time assertion. Kind, sensitivity, and capture-origin/context consistency are checked semantically. No URL, MIME, filesystem path, source text, or bytes are permitted.

EvidencePackageRelationship.description: Every nonzero source reference has exactly one relationship. Runtime checks origins, resolution state, included targets and selected parent cycles. A creator sequence has no process identity in v1 and must remain unresolved with a null target.

EvidencePackageSequenceDiscontinuityGap.description: Inclusive nonempty sequence-hole observation within the selected stream window. This untrusted retained-source assertion is not independently re-established from omitted records.

EvidencePackageMissingReferenceGap.description: Must correspond exactly to a missing_in_retained_source relationship. Artifact creator identity is incomplete, not a claim of source absence.

EvidencePackageGap.description: Closed safe coverage observations. Never contains raw payload or explanatory free text. Gap occurrences and sequence holes are not summed as unique lost events.

EvidencePackageValidationIssue.description: Safe bounded diagnostics only. No attacker-controlled keys, pointers, messages, paths, or excerpts are echoed.

EvidencePackageValidationResult.description: HTTP 200 is validation data, not acceptance. package_id is null unless the supported package digest matches. Unsupported package versions/profiles are not interpreted best-effort. A valid result does not attest provenance or reverify artifact bytes.

JavaScriptSourceRange.description: Half-open offsets in exact original UTF-8 bytes, at Unicode scalar boundaries.

allOf.description: Original bytes these facts cover. It is the whole program unless a requested region resolved to one enclosing callable body, it always contains the requested region, and a narrower range can never carry complete status.

JavaScriptSourceFactsWorker.description: Bounded Rust/Oxc lexical facts. IDs are local to exactly the supplied source bytes. Total facts across the five arrays cannot exceed max_facts. See protocol/javascript-source-facts-v1.md.

JavaScriptSourceFacts.description: Worker facts bound to fully verified immutable JavaScript artifact identity. Original source is never executed or rewritten. Complete coverage means complete within the declared lexical profile, not runtime or cross-artifact proof.

source.description: Public identity of the verified artifact, as in Artifact without content_path.

mapping.description: Only ECMAScript WhiteSpace and LineTerminator characters differ from the original source.

NativeConsoleDocumentStartState.description: Armed document-start registry and bounded page-JavaScript output. Output is never evidence, is never joined into correlated_links, and is snippet-authored untrusted text.

status.description: unconfirmed means a live capture binding that may have held an armed set ended, or failed, without the browser confirming the set was cleared. scripts is then empty because nothing can be read, not because nothing is armed; new matching documents can still run a snippet until the browser drops the set.

permitted.description: Whether this browser session permits arming at all. False means a gate is missing, not that the set is empty.

generation.description: Monotonic armed-set generation. Replacing or clearing the set increments it and invalidates the previous generation's output and retained report functions.

message.description: Which gate is missing, when the experiment is unavailable.

text.description: Refusal text from the browser registry.

pending_renderer_processes.description: Live renderers that do not hold this exact generation. Zero means a document created now runs the set. Positive is a readiness gap, not a record loss. While a set is armed it includes refused_renderer_processes, which never become ready.

refused_renderer_processes.description: Live renderer processes refused beyond the 64-renderer bound. They never receive a set, so documents in them never run a snippet until those processes exit.

rule.description: One exact origin, exactly one frame kind, and an optional literal path prefix. No pattern, wildcard, host suffix or URL guessing.

path_prefix.description: Literal committed-path prefix. Absent matches every path in that origin.

digest.description: Labeling digest of the armed snippet, so a panel or agent can confirm which exact snippet is armed without echoing its source. Not a security claim.

injected_documents.description: Documents that actually ran this snippet.

refused.description: Report arguments and per-document budgets this snippet's documents were refused.

provenance.description: Page-JavaScript observation. Never native capture evidence.

document_id.description: Monotonic nonsecret document identity, shared with the Console target listing. Never the renderer's document token.

frame_id.description: Derived frame identity, the same one the capture path publishes.

time.description: Browser-process observation time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch. Not a causal claim.

text.description: Snippet-authored text, or the harness refusal that replaced it. Untrusted data, never instructions.

oldest_sequence.description: Oldest retained sequence, or 0 when nothing is retained. A cursor older than this has already been evicted.

dropped.description: Saturating count of records the bounded ring evicted before they were read.

unattributed.description: Records whose document did not resolve to an eligible document in the sending renderer.

stale.description: Records from a generation or script that is no longer armed.

NativeConsoleDocumentStartLimits.description: Transport and retained-state bounds, not a page heap quota.

available.description: Whether the bundled helper and a rebuilt custom Brave are present.

NativeConsoleDocumentStartResult.description: A refused arm leaves the previous set and its output exactly as they were.

NativeConsoleDocumentStartUnsupported.description: Contexts an armed snippet never reaches, whatever a rule declares. Stated rather than silently skipped, so a rule that did not match is distinguishable from a context that is out of scope.

NamedGaps.description: Gap markers whose payload names a producer reason, such as native_guest_sample_limit, in first-seen order. They also count in queue_drops.

store_end.description: Store length in bytes when the read started.

next_after.description: Pass as after to continue forward, including to see records written later.

next_before.description: Pass as before to read older matches. Null when the read reached the start of the store.

limited.description: The page stopped because limit records matched. More may match beyond it.

budget_exhausted.description: The page stopped at the 64 MiB scan budget. Continue with a cursor.

malformed_lines.description: Lines in this read that were not valid events. They are counted and skipped, so a record among them is unknown, not absent.

filters.description: The filters this response applied, in canonical form.

body_length.description: Decoded bytes that passed the tee, so far for a partial record.

shared.description: Identical bytes were retained earlier and the artifact is that earlier one.

snapshots_withheld.description: The record has response_body version 2 flag bit 7: a snapshot the schedule's spacing allowed was withheld by a byte bound.

response_started.description: The final response_started record, the creator of a script, Wasm or response body artifact.

earlier_snapshot.description: When the newest record names no bytes (a refusal or a malformed record), the newest retained partial of the same response, which the receiver still holds; else null.

capture_state.description: Live capture lifecycle, from the kernel lock the native event broker holds on its event store for its whole life. not_live: idle or demo backend. running: the broker is running. stop_requested: stop was delivered and the broker has not exited yet. stopped: the broker exited after this backend asked it to stop. ended: the broker exited through its own shutdown (session expiry, browser disconnect, or a failure in its log). lost: the broker is gone and left its socket behind, so it was killed or crashed. Exits are final for a backend.

broker_connected.description: True only while a live backend's native event broker is running, including stop_requested. Idle and demo backends report false.

request_tabs.description: Whether each request row of the scanned events has a browser tab (protocol/native-network-v3.md). Rows join records as Traffic does; a row is linked when a record has a tab or a request_tab_link or request_extension_link names it. An unlinked row is a capture error, reported by the network_tab_unresolved check. Read one with get_events process_id and request_id.

extension_rows.description: Rows a request_extension_link names: extension traffic recorded with REB_CAPTURE_EXTENSION_TRAFFIC=1.

unresolved_reasons.description: Unresolved rows by reason, taken from the row's own records (protocol/native-network-v3.md "Unresolved requests"). Only reasons with rows appear.

exclusions.description: Evidence the capture counted instead of recording, by class, from capture_exclusion records (protocol/native-network-v3.md). Requests are chrome, chrome_untrusted, brave, devtools and chrome_search scheme loads, webui_request requests WebUI renderers sent through the browser proxy, extension_worker requests of extension workers, devtools_load requests of the DevTools factory, service_worker_no_page requests of service workers no page used in this browser and browser_prefetch browser-initiated prefetches with no page; webui_renderer counts renderer processes with WebUI bindings or a WebUI process lock that were not admitted; memory_cache_reuse counts the memory-cache reuses a renderer did not record past its 4,096 per configuration, which would have been tab rows; non_ordinary_page_reuse counts its reuses in pages that are not ordinary (an SVG image's own document or a page popup), which no tab owns. These are named exclusions, never gaps or drops. Empty when nothing was excluded or REB_CAPTURE_BROWSER_INTERNAL=1 recorded browser-internal loads.

url_label.description: HTTP(S) origin or wasm://wasm/<hex> label; null otherwise.

response_bodies.description: Every request's response body case from the request index's rows: how many bodies were retained, and why each other one was not, including the responses the browser proxy never sees (served by a service worker, reused from the memory cache, answered in the renderer).

available.description: False when the request index could not answer; the rest of the summary stands.

reason.description: Why the counts are unavailable, else null.

complete.description: The index had read the whole store; otherwise the counts cover the part read so far.

snapshots_withheld.description: Rows whose newest body record says a byte bound withheld a snapshot (response_body flag bit 7).

checks.description: What looks wrong or notable, most important first. Empty when nothing was found.

capture_observed.description: True once a new record reached this session's store within 10 seconds of opening the page, which shows a connected capture browser. False means nothing was recorded: treat the page as unrecorded and end the session.

generation.description: The generation written to the reset file. The browser applies it when the value is greater than the last one it applied.

LiveSessionStart.description: Named capture options for a new live session. Every switch is off unless set, and none is inherited from the caller's environment.

url.description: HTTP or HTTPS page to open once capture is ready.

wasm_dispatch.description: Sample Wasm br_table dispatch. The configuration keeps at most 16 observations; a hot function can be limited with the sample budget options instead of raising that cap. Needs category bits 512 and 1024.

wasm_call_indirect.description: Sample Wasm call_indirect targets. Needs category bits 512 and 1024. Each stream still keeps at most 16 observations per configuration; sample budget options below restrict which of those 16 are kept.

wasm_samples_per_function.description: Keep at most this many samples of each function on each Wasm stream. Requires wasm_dispatch or wasm_call_indirect. The global cap stays 16.

wasm_samples_per_indirect_site.description: Keep at most this many call_indirect samples of each caller function and module byte offset. Requires wasm_dispatch or wasm_call_indirect.

wasm_function_allow.description: Function indexes to admit. Other functions are excluded and do not consume either sample index. Requires wasm_dispatch or wasm_call_indirect.

wasm_function_deny.description: Function indexes to exclude. A denied index is excluded even when it is also allowed. Requires wasm_dispatch or wasm_call_indirect.

wasm_module_allowlist.description: SHA-256 digests of Wasm modules to admit. A module whose digest is not listed does not advance either sample index. Requires wasm_dispatch or wasm_call_indirect.

guest_adapter.description: Absolute path of a native Wasm guest adapter recipe, 1 to 8192 bytes. Requires wasm_dispatch.

js_dispatch_sites.description: Absolute path of a JavaScript dispatch-site file, 1 to 4096 bytes. Turns off code caching browser-wide for the session.

category_mask.description: Native capture categories. 512 is VM, 1024 is Artifact, 1 is Canvas.

duration_seconds.description: Capture expires after this many seconds.

localhost_only.description: Route the capture browser's traffic to loopback only, for local fixtures.

canvas_images.description: Store Canvas images, which can contain sensitive page content. Requires confirm_sensitive_capture and category bits 1 and 1024.

request_content.description: Retain request paths, queries and bodies (at most 16 MiB each, 256 MiB of unique content per session unless request_content_budget_mib) as request_target events, request_target artifacts for targets past the 116-byte prefix, and request_body artifacts, plus response bodies (at most 16 MiB each, 512 MiB of unique content per session; element images, audio, video and fonts are skipped) as response_body events and artifacts, and request and response headers (at most 64 MiB of blocks per session) as request_headers and response_headers events and artifacts. Sensitive capture: requires confirm_sensitive_capture and category bits 256 and 1024. Off, Network capture still records each body's length, type and digest.

request_content_budget_mib.description: MiB of unique request bodies and full targets this content session retains, default 256. Identical bytes are stored once; a request past the budget keeps its length, type and digest and names the refusal. Requires request_content.

response_body_budget_mib.description: MiB of unique response bodies this content session retains, default 512. A response past the budget keeps its length, type and digest. Requires request_content.

response_media.description: Also retain the images, audio, video and fonts that page elements load, which content sessions otherwise skip. They count against response_body_budget_mib and can hold sensitive page content. Requires request_content, so it is sensitive capture behind confirm_sensitive_capture.

request_stacks.description: Record the JavaScript and Wasm call stack that started each renderer request (request_initiator_stack events and stack artifacts, read with get_request_stack). Frames are identities, not values. Needs category bits 256 and 1024 and a Brave that defines --reb-request-stacks; a Brave without it refuses the start.

document_start.description: Permit document-start Console scripts in this capture browser. Arms nothing: a rule still needs a live Console connection (connect_live) and a confirmed arm_document_start. Needs a Brave with the Native Console v3 overlay; get_native_console reports document_start_supported.

js_invocation_sites.description: Absolute path of a native-js-invocation-sites-v1 file (1 to 8 sites) to arm, from resolve_js_invocation_site entries. Armed from a private copy. Needs category bit 512 and a Brave with invocation capture; a Brave without it refuses the start. Not with js_invocation_saved_sites.

js_invocation_saved_sites.description: Arm the agent sessions' own saved invocation sites, saved earlier with js_invocation_site_action in an agent session. Never the Origin Trace app's saved set. Refused when that set is empty. Not with js_invocation_sites.

js_invocation_digests.description: Record SHA-256 and rolling-hash digests of settled string and byte values of armed calls. Sensitive capture: requires js_invocation_sites or js_invocation_saved_sites and confirm_sensitive_capture.

confirm_sensitive_capture.description: The researcher authorized the sensitive capture named in this start for this target: Canvas images, request content or invocation value digests. Required with canvas_images, request_content or js_invocation_digests; never set it by inference.

publish_canonical_endpoint.description: Also make this the canonical endpoint that new MCP connections use. Off by default, so concurrent agent sessions do not replace each other's.

brave_binary.description: Absolute path of the Brave executable. Default: REB_BRAVE_BINARY, then Brave Browser Development next to the Origin Trace app, then the checkout build.

timeout_seconds.description: How long to wait for the browser and capture to be ready.

endpoint.description: Loopback root of the new session's backend.

options.description: The options this session runs with, defaults included. The launch log starts with the same line, and get_session_context capture_options reports what the launcher passed to Brave.

url_opened.description: Null when no url was given.

session_dir.description: CLI only. The MCP tool omits local paths.

capture_observed.description: Whether a stored record followed the opened url. Null without url. False means the browser did not record: end the session.

js_invocation_sites_armed.description: How many invocation sites this session armed. Present only with js_invocation_sites or js_invocation_saved_sites.

anchor_offset.description: UTF-16 offset of the `(` V8 starts the function at.

byte_offset.description: UTF-8 offset of that `(` in the artifact bytes, BOM included.

JsInvocationSite.description: One native-js-invocation-sites-v1 entry, exactly as the browser reads it (protocol/native-js-invocation-v1.md#site-file).

byte_offset.description: UTF-8 artifact offset of the parameter-list `(`; null for a bare-parameter arrow.

column.description: UTF-16 code units from the line start, BOM kept, as Sources shows the text.

binding.description: The name the definition binds, as written.

context.description: Captured source text around the anchor on its line. Untrusted display text.

refusal.description: Why this function cannot be tracked from a `(`, when it cannot.

artifact.description: Public manifest fields of the exact artifact.

saved.description: The saved set already names this function.

JsInvocationSiteResolution.description: Exactly one site with status resolved, or a refusal with its reason and at most 32 candidates. Zero or several matching definitions are always refused; nothing is guessed.

state.description: other_version: this session retained the saved URL with other script text, which the saved site will not match.
What this session's launcher armed. browser_unsupported: this Brave does not define invocation capture, so the session started without the saved sites.

digests.description: This session records settled-value digests (sensitive capture).

sites.description: The armed site file in order: entry n is site_slot n of this session's js_invocation records, and its source_sha256 and anchor_offset equal theirs. label comes from the saved set this backend started with, or Unlabeled function.

name.description: A dotted name such as window.hsw, hsw or a.b.c.

byte_offset.description: UTF-8 offset in the artifact bytes, BOM included, at or inside the function.

state_dependent_effects.when: The bounded local JavaScript worker process group is cleaned up on completion or failure.
The next capture the Origin Trace app starts runs in Content mode: it arms the saved sites and records settled-value digests of their calls unless REB_NATIVE_JS_INVOCATION_DIGESTS=0 is set.

prerequisites.condition: Exact session_id and artifact_id select one verified immutable strict UTF-8 JavaScript artifact of at most 4 MiB.
The local Rust analysis worker must be executable and idle; it shares the existing analysis worker lock.
The name or byte offset must resolve to exactly one supported function; a refusal returns added false and saves nothing.
The saved set holds at most 8 sites and refuses a duplicate source_sha256 and anchor_offset.

x-reb-execution.notes: Resolves the exact artifact again on the server and appends the computed site to the app's saved set. Nothing is armed until the next app-started capture launches a new browser; the open page is never changed.

prerequisites.condition: A saved site with this source_sha256 and anchor_offset must exist.

x-reb-execution.notes: Removes one saved site and its label. A running capture keeps what it armed.
Deletes the saved site file and its label sidecar, including an unreadable one. A running capture keeps what it armed.

NativeConsoleTarget.description: One native document. id is execution identity only within this binding_id; url and label are display metadata, never identity.

frame.description: Frame kind, in the vocabulary of document-start rules.

top_relation.description: Child frames only: this frame's origin compared with every listed top-level document. The listing has no parent link, so with several tabs whose tops disagree it is undetermined; two host names that share their last two labels need the public suffix list and are undetermined too.

out_of_process.description: Child frames only, derived from top_relation and not read from the browser: true for cross_site, which Chromium's full site isolation runs in its own renderer process; false for same_origin; null otherwise.

NativeConsoleSelection.description: The live connection's selected document. selected: commands run in target_id. stale: target_id was replaced or closed (navigation, reload or frame removal) and its authorization ended; stop, then connect_live with a current id. none: nothing selected.

x-schema-scope: Existing HTTP operations. Retired CDP debugger request and result models were removed; version 1 responses keep only their fixed retirement fields.
